children: Stock futures were sliding on Tuesday as investors carried on worrying about the bond market selloff, with the yield on the 10-year Treasury note topping 4.8%.

Dell jumped 9% ahead of the opening bell after the hardware company's second-quarter earnings and revenue topped analysts' expectations, as the artificial-intelligence boom drives up demand for its products.
Palo Alto Networks slid 1.7%. The cybersecurity company reported strong fourth-quarter earnings, but investors still opted to take profit with shares up 97% for the year through Tuesday's close.

Credo sank 8.7%, even though the electrical cable maker's first-quarter results beat expectations. The revenue beat and guidance "seems a bit skinnier" than in previous quarters, Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein said.

GitLab soared 20% after the coding platform's second-quarter earnings came in well above Wall Street's target, easing fears about fierce competition from the likes of Microsoft's GitHub and SpaceX's Cursor.
MongoDB slumped 13% after second-quarter revenue for the document database company's multi-cloud service Atlas grew at a slower pace than some hedge funds were expecting.
Chip maker Broadcom, cloud-computing company Snowflake, and server maker Hewlett Packard Enterprise are set to report earnings after Wednesday's close.
